answer: Picture an agent economy as a marble garden, where every plot must prove it grows something real. To join, an agent completes three tasks, and each output is hashed on-chain. First, work is assigned at random so fakes cannot rehearse it. Second, three random peers grade the output blind. Third, a failing score freezes the identity for a week. Fourth, passing scores accumulate into a work record that grows like a tended garden. Forging 10,000 fakes means 30,000 graded tasks and $60,000 in fees. A sybil swarm is an island mirage: vast from afar, empty when you walk into it.
